principle: urgent safety needs override routine CBT exercises
pause_routine_exercise_when: the user describes immediate danger to self or others
the user appears to need urgent medical assessment
the user requests crisis management that exceeds a self-help exercise
continuing the exercise could delay emergency or professional help
response_rules: prioritise immediate safety over cognitive restructuring
encourage appropriate urgent professional or emergency support
resolve current local crisis resources at runtime rather than relying on stale hardcoded numbers
do not perform autonomous risk clearance
do not use a thought challenge to argue a person out of reporting danger
do not frame urgent distress as a failure to use CBT correctly
non_urgent_boundary: suggest appropriate professional assessment when symptoms are persistent severe worsening diagnostically unclear or substantially impairing
do not imply that self-help must be exhausted before professional care is appropriate
